slides.title: What Is a Delegate?
slides.content: A delegate is a type that holds a reference to a method (or methods) with a matching signature. Think of it as a function pointer that the type system can check at compile time.

options: a type that references a method
exercise.answer: a type that references a method

slides.title: Multicast Delegates
slides.content: A delegate can hold a list of methods. Subscribing with += adds a method; invoking the delegate runs every added method in order and returns the last value.
slides.exampleOutput: (Add and Subtract both run; r is the last return value)

options: calls all methods in the list
returns the sum of the results
exercise.answer: calls all methods in the list

slides.title: Lambda Expressions
slides.content: A lambda (=>) is a concise inline method. You can assign it to a delegate type to create the method on the spot instead of naming a separate method.
slides.example:
Calculator calc = (x, y) => x + y;
int r = calc(3, 4);

slides.title: Func and Action
slides.content: Func<...> represents a function that returns a value (the last type parameter is the return type). Action<...> represents a delegate that returns void.
slides.example:
Func<int, int, int> add = (x, y) => x + y;
Action<string> print = s => Console.WriteLine(s);

slides.title: Events
slides.content: An event is a delegate field exposed for subscribe/unsubscribe. The event keyword prevents external code from assigning to the event or invoking it directly; only the declaring class can raise it.
slides.exampleOutput: (subscribers can += or -=; external code cannot assign OnChange = ...)

options: external code from assigning the event field directly
exercise.answer: external code from assigning the event field directly

slides.title: Subscribing and Unsubscribing
slides.content: Attach a handler with += and detach it with -=. The handler must match the delegate's signature (parameters and return type).

exercise.prompt: A handler is attached to an event with the _____ operator.

slides.title: The EventHandler Pattern
slides.content: The standard .NET convention passes (object sender, EventArgs e). Custom data uses an EventArgs subclass as the second argument.
slides.exampleOutput: (sender is the publisher, e is the event data)

exercise.prompt: Raise the event from inside the class.
hints: Invoke the event by its name.
Pass this as the sender and EventArgs.Empty as the args.

slides.title: Delegates Review
slides.content: Delegates are types referencing methods; lambdas assign inline; events expose safe subscribe/unsubscribe; Func/Action are built-in delegate types for common signatures.

exercise.prompt: Assign a lambda that doubles x, then the result is 10.
hints: Assign a lambda such as (x => x * 2).
